messages:
alice: Heads-up — nightly job caught a small perf regression on the kv-cache hot path (p50 token latency +7%). I ran a quick nsys on a single run and saw heavier memcpy+kernel churn around kv-lookup kernels. Can we automate trace capture and diffing in CI?
ben: yep we should. do you have a reproducible config? sample input and seed? :eyes:
alice: repro in `perf/e2e/kv_burst.yaml` (batch sizes 1,8,32; seq_len 1024). short cmd: `./run_perf.sh --cfg perf/e2e/kv_burst.yaml --seed 42`. failing commit is in main ~ea2f9.
carla: I can add an nsys wrapper step. plan: run 3 iterations per job (warm, baseline, candidate) and collect `nvtx` ranges so we can correlate host<->device. Use `nsys profile --output ${OUT} --trace=cuda,osrt,cudnn --capture-range=nvtx` then upload.
david: storage note — keep nightly traces for 14 days in S3 then move to Glacier if retained. we need size limits per-run (try to cap to 500MB).
perf-bot: existing job `perf/nightly/basic` runs unit perf only. propose new workflow `perf/nightly/traces` that triggers on schedule and optionally on PR with label `perf-trace`.
carla: rough GH Actions snippet I'm going to try:```name: ci-trace
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * *' # daily
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled]

jobs:
  capture:
    runs-on: self-hosted-gpu
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: run nsys
        run: |
          mkdir -p traces
          nsys profile --output traces/trace-${{ github.run_id }} --trace=cuda,osrt --capture-range=nvtx ./run_perf.sh --cfg perf/e2e/kv_burst.yaml --seed 42
      - name: upload
        run: aws s3 cp traces/ s3://redwood-perf-nightly/${{ github.run_id }}/ --recursive```
ben: +1. also add a small sampling harness so we don't always run full seq_len=1024. pick 10% runs with long-seq and 90% short. we should record config metadata (kernel selection flags, quantization profile, batcher window) to JSON alongside traces.
alice: good call. also include `nvprof --print-gpu-trace` fallback for dev hosts that don't have nsys. and capture `dmesg`/`nvidia-smi --query` output.
david: for diffs, we can extract kernel timelines and generate a compact summary: kernel name, total time, invocations, avg duration. store as CSV/Parquet. downstream dashboard (perf-ui) can diff two runs and highlight regressions >5% and new kernels.
carla: implementation detail: in the nsys postprocess step run:```nsys stats traces/trace-*.qdrep --report gputrace --format csv -o traces/summary.csv
python tools/parse_nsys.py traces/summary.csv traces/summary.json --fields kernel_name,total_time,invocations,avg_time
# upload both json and raw qdrep
aws s3 cp traces/summary.json s3://redwood-perf-nightly/${{ github.run_id }}/```
perf-bot: once uploaded we can kick a lambda to run diff against yesterday's summary and emit a short report to #eng-runtime with tags and links. include lightweight flamegraph images (SVG) for quick triage.
david: permission checklist: ensure S3 bucket has write-only creds for CI and a separate read role for the UI. add lifecycle rule and kms encryption.
alice: next steps: carla to open PR for GH Action + parse script; david to add S3 lifecycle + IAM; ben to wire config meta + sampling; I'll prepare a short postmortem-ish note if this was an actual regression to track root cause.
carla: will do, assigning myself. ping me if you want a demo trace viewer. :rocket:
